direct_flood_classifier_assessment.reason: All seven candidates remain UNKNOWN and training-ineligible. No flood outcome labels may be fabricated from rainfall, susceptibility, or missing reports.
direct_flood_classifier_assessment.decision: Do not train or represent a direct flood classifier in the current evidence state.

pipeline: TensorFlow regression for future rainfall quantity
Separately governed static MGB flood susceptibility
Distinct Module 1 display of rainfall forecast, susceptibility, and combined assessment
hybrid_architecture_assessment.model_claim: TensorFlow would predict rainfall quantity, not learned flood occurrence, until governed flood outcome labels exist.
hybrid_architecture_assessment.required_separation: The deterministic fusion layer must not be presented as TensorFlow flood classification or as a probability calibrated from flood outcomes.

recommended_rainfall_target.construction: Sum six future verified 30-minute IMERG interval accumulations immediately after the forecast origin.
recommended_rainfall_target.why: A 3-hour quantity is responsive enough for emergency research while reducing single-interval noise and avoiding the stronger operational assumptions of a 24-hour flood target.

alternatives_not_selected.next_30_minutes: Too noisy for a first emergency-risk research component.
alternatives_not_selected.next_1_hour: Viable secondary benchmark but less stable than a 3-hour accumulation.
alternatives_not_selected.next_6_hours: Useful secondary benchmark but less responsive for short-horizon action.
alternatives_not_selected.next_24_hours: Too close to the existing flood target and more vulnerable to broad accumulation assumptions.

input_design.feature_timestamps: Only verified observed intervals ending at or before the forecast origin may enter inputs.

spatial_design.approach_reason: A city-level rainfall series matches the current city-level evidence better than locality claims, limits neighbor contamination, and prevents 16 cells from being mistaken for 16 disasters.
spatial_design.area_weighting: Not selected until the existing authoritative polygons and IMERG cell footprints are implemented and independently reviewed for coverage weights.
spatial_design.cell_level_option: The 16 cells may be modeled as correlated channels or spatial features, but never as independent event labels. Splits must be chronological and keep all cells from a timestamp in the same split.

recommended_next_phase_range.duration: Approximately 12 months plus the governed Enteng endpoint
recommended_next_phase_range.spatial_scope: The three Caloocan-intersecting 0.1-degree centers, with the existing 16-cell set retained only for bounded sensitivity analysis

historical_corpus_requirement.reason: One continuous wet/dry seasonal cycle is the shortest bounded corpus likely to expose seasonality, antecedent persistence, and non-event rainfall variation without claiming a universal sample-size threshold.
historical_corpus_requirement.required_separation: Use chronological train/validation/test periods; keep all cells and overlapping windows from a timestamp in one split.

mgb_risk_fusion.not_automatic_mapping: Do not map LF/MF/HF/VHF directly to LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/CRITICAL without a separately documented policy.
required_governance: Preserve MGB category and attribution independently.
Version any deterministic fusion policy and its thresholds.
Keep rainfall forecast quantity visibly separate from susceptibility.
Do not call fused output a calibrated flood probability without labeled outcome validation.
Require human and operational review before activation.

separate_outputs: MGB susceptibility: static LF/MF/HF/VHF/NONE with source attribution
TensorFlow rainfall forecast: predicted precipitation quantity in mm over the proposed horizon
Combined application flood-risk assessment: deterministic, versioned policy output with explicit provenance
module_1_output_design.ui_requirement: Never imply that MGB susceptibility or a rainfall forecast alone is a flood outcome label or that both are the same TensorFlow prediction.

proposed_periods.training: First 70% of the recommended one-year-plus corpus

leakage_controls: No future timestamps in input features.
No overlapping windows across split boundaries.
All spatial cells for a timestamp remain in one split.
Fit normalization parameters on training period only.

tensorflow_architecture.reason: It is the simplest auditable baseline for a one-year bounded corpus and avoids assuming that LSTM/GRU complexity is justified.

comparison.small_dense: Primary baseline; transparent parameter count and lag attribution.
comparison.one_dimensional_temporal_model: Secondary comparison if the dense baseline cannot capture local temporal structure.
comparison.lstm_gru: Defer until the chronological corpus and baseline justify sequence-model complexity.

capstone_compatibility.path_b_interpretation: TensorFlow-Based Rainfall Forecasting with governed deterministic Flood-Risk Fusion
documentation_concerns: The capstone must not claim TensorFlow learned flood occurrence without flood outcome labels.
Risk fusion must be documented as a separate deterministic governance/application layer.
Any probability language must be removed or reserved for a future labeled calibration phase.
The existing FLOOD_WITHIN_24H target and four risk categories remain pending and must not be silently redefined.
capstone_compatibility.future_documentation_action: Propose a terminology decision before implementation: rainfall prediction component versus direct flood classifier.

remaining_blockers: No governed flood-positive or affirmative negative labels.
No formally adjudicated prediction cutoff or final target.
Only 72 hours of Enteng rainfall is available, insufficient for robust rainfall regression.
No approved training authorization for rainfall modeling.
No documented deterministic fusion thresholds or operational policy.
